svg.title: GRIP pipeline: from continuous phenotype to ranked gene candidates
svg.desc: RNA sequencing and continuous Oil Red O measurements enter a filtered, transformed, sample-grouped regression pipeline. Conventional and invariant models generate predictions and feature evidence. Mode-filtered models contribute to gene scoring, followed by biological annotation, enrichment and sensitivity analyses. Dimensions reflect one saved local reconstruction.

g.text: From continuous phenotype to ranked gene candidates
A regression and invariance workflow for RNA-seq · architecture grounded in the local implementation
Same samples supply X and y.
Join expression and metadata by ID
Keep count matrix and phenotype aligned
All views of one sample stay together
Fit scaler on training rows only
X and continuous y retained in every view
Saved run: PFI with three repeats
Saved run: keep top 3 invariant models
F: selection frequency; I: mean importance
Q̄: common quality factor for this run
Keep component scores and model provenance
Top-20 set and full gene ranking
CSV evidence, model metrics, run config
Map Ensembl IDs to gene symbols
Interpret functions and curated gene sets
Compare GRIP and CRISP candidate sets
Research follow-up, not a completed result
62 sample IDs · 12,081 genes · 6 views · 12 technical environments · 48 / 7 / 7 split · seed 42
Voting-set R²: nonlinear ICP −1.23; nonlinear IRM −1.79; linear ICP −1.86. Random Forest R² = 0.218 was excluded by invariant mode.
Evaluation note: grouping copies and fitting the scaler on train do not establish a fully leakage-free pipeline; data-adaptive transforms and selection need independent evaluation.
Source: local GRIP source + full_osdr_recreation configuration, log and artifacts (saved July 9, 2026). Architecture illustration; matrix colors are schematic.
